1. Purpose and Scope
This handbook governs orientation, mandatory training, competency validation, and continuing education (CE)
requirements for all clinical and non-clinical staff of Meridian Valley General Hospital. It applies to employees,
contracted staff, students, and volunteers.
2. New Employee Orientation Program
2.1 Orientation Schedule
All new hires complete a mandatory 3-day General Orientation within their first week of employment, followed
by department-specific orientation lasting 2-10 days depending on role complexity.

2.2 Department-Specific Orientation
Following General Orientation, employees report to their assigned unit for preceptor-guided orientation. Clinical
staff must complete unit-specific skills checklists before working independent shifts. Preceptors document
competency sign-off in the Learning Management System (LMS).

3. Mandatory Annual Training (All Staff)
●
HIPAA Privacy & Security Refresher (30 min, LMS module EDU-101)
●
Fire and Life Safety / RACE-PASS Fire Extinguisher Review (30 min)
●
Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Control (30 min, required for roles with exposure risk)

●
Workplace Violence Prevention & De-escalation (45 min)
●
Cultural Competency and Health Equity (30 min)
●
Corporate Compliance and Anti-Kickback / Stark Law Overview (30 min)
●
Emergency Preparedness: Hospital Incident Command System (HICS) Overview (30 min)
Completion deadline: all modules must be finished by the employee's hire-date anniversary each year.
Non-completion beyond a 30-day grace period results in automatic LMS escalation to the employee's manager
and, if unresolved after 60 days, restriction of EHR access pending completion.

5. Continuing Education (CE) Support
●
Nursing staff: 20 CE hours/year required for license renewal; hospital reimburses up to $750/year for
approved external courses or conferences.
●
Physicians: CME tracked via Medical Staff Office; minimum 50 CME credits per 2-year privileging cycle.
●
Allied health (RT, PT, OT, Pharmacy): CE requirements per state licensing board, tracked in LMS.
●
Internal Grand Rounds held every Thursday 12:00-1:00 PM in the Auditorium; 1 CE credit per session.
●
Tuition assistance program: up to $5,250/year for degree programs relevant to current or planned role,

●
Tuition assistance program: up to $5,250/year for degree programs relevant to current or planned role,
requires 1-year service commitment post-completion.
6. Simulation Center
The Clinical Simulation Center (Building C, 2nd Floor) offers high-fidelity manikin labs, a mock patient room,
and a task-trainer library for procedural skills (suturing, intubation, central line placement, lumbar puncture).
Units may book the center via the Education Department scheduling portal. Interprofessional simulation (rapid
response, code blue, mass casualty drills) is run quarterly for each inpatient unit.

7. Learning Management System (LMS) Access
All staff access the LMS at learn.meridianvalley-demo.org using their network credentials. Managers can pull
completion reports for their teams under Reports > Compliance Dashboard. Questions about assigned modules
should be directed to education@meridianvalley-demo.org or extension 4420.

1. Purpose and Scope
This manual establishes operating procedures for the Facilities Engineering & Plant Operations department,
responsible for the physical plant, utility systems, life-safety systems, and maintenance of all buildings at
Meridian Valley General Hospital (Main Hospital, Medical Office Building, Central Utility Plant, and Parking
Structure).
2. Work Order System

3. Critical Utility Systems
3.1 Emergency Power
Three 1,500 kW diesel generators provide backup power to life-safety branch, critical branch, and equipment
branch circuits per NFPA 99/110. Generators are load-tested monthly (30 min under load) and undergo a full
4-hour annual load bank test. Automatic transfer switches (ATS) are inspected quarterly. Fuel reserves are
maintained for a minimum 96-hour run time.
3.2 Medical Gas Systems
Oxygen, medical air, and vacuum systems are monitored 24/7 via the Building Automation System (BAS) with

3.2 Medical Gas Systems
Oxygen, medical air, and vacuum systems are monitored 24/7 via the Building Automation System (BAS) with
alarm panels at the Plant Operations control room and Nursing Supervisor station. Master alarm signals must
be investigated within 10 minutes. Annual certification testing is performed per NFPA 99 by a certified medical
gas verifier.
3.3 HVAC and Air Handling

Operating rooms and isolation rooms are monitored for pressure relationships (positive for OR/protective
isolation, negative for airborne infection isolation) with continuous differential pressure monitors. Air changes
per hour (ACH) are validated semi-annually: OR minimum 20 ACH (4 fresh), AII rooms minimum 12 ACH.

5. Life Safety and Interim Life Safety Measures (ILSM)
Any construction, renovation, or system impairment that affects fire/life safety triggers an ILSM assessment
(Form ENG-LS-04) before work begins, covering temporary egress routes, fire watch requirements,
dust/infection control barriers (per ICRA matrix), and notification of Nursing Administration and the Safety
Officer.
6. Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) for Construction
All construction and renovation projects require an ICRA permit classifying the project (Type A-D) and required
precautions (Class I-IV), jointly signed off by Facilities, Infection Prevention, and the affected unit manager
before work begins.
7. Utility Failure Response
●
Power failure: Confirm generator start and ATS transfer within 10 seconds; notify House Supervisor and

7. Utility Failure Response
●
Power failure: Confirm generator start and ATS transfer within 10 seconds; notify House Supervisor and
Nursing Administration immediately; log event in CMMS.
●
Water disruption: Activate Water Outage Plan (bottled water carts, portable handwash stations); notify
Infection Prevention and affected units.
●
Medical gas alarm: Dispatch engineer to source location within 10 minutes; do not silence alarm until cause
confirmed and corrected.
●
HVAC failure in OR/isolation room: Suspend use of affected room until pressure relationships and air changes
are restored and verified.

 General Hospital Rules & Code of Conduct
Document ID: ADM-GR-002   |   Effective Date: January 1, 2026   |   Owner: Chief Executive Officer, M. Delacroix-Huang
  |   Status: Active   |   This is a fictional/demo document for RAG testing purposes.
1. Purpose
These General Hospital Rules apply to all employees, medical staff, students, volunteers, contractors, patients,
and visitors at Meridian Valley General Hospital. They establish baseline expectations for conduct, safety, and
the environment of care. Department-specific policies supplement, but do not override, these rules.
2. Identification and Badges
●
All staff must wear a hospital-issued photo ID badge, visible above the waist, at all times while on hospital
premises.
●
Badges are used for building access, EHR login (badge-tap), and medication dispensing cabinet access; lost
badges must be reported to Security immediately at ext. 4000.
●

badges must be reported to Security immediately at ext. 4000.
●
Visitors must check in at the main lobby and wear a visitor sticker; visiting hours are 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM for
general units, with 24-hour access for designated support persons in Labor & Delivery, Pediatrics, and
end-of-life situations.
3. Code of Conduct
All personnel are expected to treat patients, families, and colleagues with dignity and respect. The hospital
maintains a zero-tolerance policy for the following:
●
Harassment, bullying, or discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability,
sexual orientation, gender identity, or veteran status.
●
Disruptive behavior toward staff or patients, including intimidation, yelling, or throwing objects.
●
Falsification of medical records, timekeeping records, or any official hospital document.
●
Use, possession, or being under the influence of alcohol or non-prescribed controlled substances while on
duty.

●
Unauthorized access to, use of, or disclosure of patient information (see HIPAA Privacy Policy ADM-GR-011).
4. Smoke-Free and Tobacco-Free Campus
Meridian Valley General Hospital is a 100% smoke- and tobacco-free campus, including e-cigarettes and
vaping devices. This applies to all buildings, grounds, parking structures, and hospital-owned vehicles, with no
designated outdoor smoking areas.

7. Patient Rights and Responsibilities (Summary)
Patients have the right to considerate and respectful care, to be informed about their diagnosis and treatment
options, to participate in decisions about their care, to access their medical records, to privacy and
confidentiality, and to voice grievances without fear of reprisal. The full Patient Rights and Responsibilities
statement (Form ADM-GR-003) is provided at admission and posted on every inpatient unit.
8. Grievance and Complaint Process
Patients or families may raise concerns with the care team directly, or contact Patient Relations at ext. 3300 /
patientrelations@meridianvalley-demo.org. Formal grievances are acknowledged within 7 days and resolved or
given a status update within 30 days, per policy ADM-GR-015.
9. Weapons and Prohibited Items

given a status update within 30 days, per policy ADM-GR-015.
9. Weapons and Prohibited Items
Weapons of any kind are prohibited on hospital premises for all persons other than authorized law enforcement
and hospital Security personnel. This policy applies regardless of state concealed-carry permit status,
consistent with the hospital's status as a licensed healthcare facility.

10. Parking
Employees park in designated Staff Parking Structure B using badge access; Visitor and Patient parking (Lots
A and C) are separate. Reserved spaces near the main entrance are for patient drop-off, ADA-accessible
parking, and emergency vehicles only.

4. Account Access and Password Policy

●
Passwords must be a minimum of 12 characters, including upper/lowercase, a number, and a symbol; expire
every 90 days and cannot reuse the last 10 passwords.
●
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required for all remote access, email, and privileged accounts.
●
Accounts lock after 5 failed login attempts; unlock via Service Desk with identity verification.
●
Generic/shared logins are prohibited for EHR access; each clinician uses individually issued credentials to
preserve the audit trail.
●
Access is provisioned based on role (RBAC) and reviewed quarterly by department managers; access is
automatically revoked within 24 hours of termination via the HR-IT integration feed.
5. Acceptable Use Policy (Summary)
●
Hospital systems and devices are for business use; incidental personal use is permitted if it does not interfere
with duties, consume excessive bandwidth, or violate policy.
●

with duties, consume excessive bandwidth, or violate policy.
●
Protected Health Information (PHI) may only be accessed on a need-to-know basis; browsing records out of
curiosity ("snooping") is a terminable HIPAA violation and is monitored via audit logging.
●
USB storage devices are disabled by default on clinical workstations; exceptions require Information Security
approval and device encryption.
●
Personal cloud storage (e.g., personal Dropbox/Google Drive) may not be used to store hospital data.
●
Only IT-approved software may be installed; local admin rights are restricted on clinical devices.
6. Downtime Procedures
In the event of a planned or unplanned EHR downtime, units activate the Downtime Policy (IT-BC-02):
downtime paper forms (kept in the red downtime folder on each unit) are used for orders, documentation, and
medication administration. Critical results are called directly to the unit. The Downtime Recovery Team

medication administration. Critical results are called directly to the unit. The Downtime Recovery Team
reconciles paper documentation into the EHR once systems are restored, with dual sign-off for high-alert
medications administered during downtime.
7. Cybersecurity Incident Reporting
Suspected phishing emails, malware, lost/stolen devices, or unauthorized access must be reported immediately
to the Security Operations Center at ext. 4911 or security@meridianvalley-demo.org. Do not forward suspected
phishing emails to colleagues; use the "Report Phish" button in Outlook. All hospital-issued laptops and mobile
devices are encrypted and remote-wipeable.
8. New Hardware / Software Requests
Requests for new hardware, software, or system integrations are submitted via the IT Request Portal and
require department director approval. Clinical system changes additionally require review by the Clinical
Informatics Governance Committee, which meets on the first Tuesday of each month.

This manual defines the standard workflow for registering and admitting patients at Meridian Valley General
Hospital, covering scheduled admissions, emergency department (ED) admissions, direct transfers, and
observation status placement.

3. Standard Admission Workflow
●
Step 1 - Pre-Registration: Demographics, insurance, and emergency contact captured by phone or online
patient portal 24-72 hours before a scheduled admission.
●
Step 2 - Identity Verification: Two patient identifiers required (full name + date of birth) at every check-in point,
per National Patient Safety Goal NPSG.01.01.01.
●
Step 3 - Insurance Verification & Financial Counseling: Eligibility checked in real time; patients with high
out-of-pocket balances are offered a financial counseling consult before admission.
●
Step 4 - Consent: General Consent for Treatment and Notice of Privacy Practices signed and scanned into

●
Step 4 - Consent: General Consent for Treatment and Notice of Privacy Practices signed and scanned into
the EHR. Procedure-specific informed consent obtained separately by the treating clinician.
●
Step 5 - Armband & Wristband ID: Color-coded wristbands applied (white = standard ID, red = allergy, yellow
= fall risk, purple = DNR/limited code status).
●
Step 6 - Bed Assignment: Bed Control coordinates placement based on acuity, isolation needs, and unit
census; average time from bed request to assignment target is under 45 minutes.
●
Step 7 - Handoff to Unit: Nursing report given by ED or admitting physician using SBAR format
(Situation-Background-Assessment-Recommendation).

6. Minor and Unaccompanied Patient Admissions
Patients under 18 require a parent or legal guardian to sign consent, except in emergencies where the

6. Minor and Unaccompanied Patient Admissions
Patients under 18 require a parent or legal guardian to sign consent, except in emergencies where the
Emancipated Minor or Emergency Treatment Doctrine applies. Unaccompanied minors are held in a supervised
area and Social Work is notified immediately per policy ADM-C-09.
7. Bed Control and Census Management
The Bed Control Center (ext. 3100, staffed 24/7) manages real-time bed status across all 312 licensed beds.
Units update bed status in the EHR bed board within 15 minutes of a discharge, transfer, or admission. Daily
bed huddles occur at 8:00 AM, 12:00 PM, and 4:00 PM involving charge nurses, Bed Control, and the House
Supervisor.
8. Discharge & Transfer Coordination
Anticipated discharge date (ADD) is documented within 24 hours of admission and updated daily on
interdisciplinary rounds. Case Management screens all admissions within 24 hours for discharge planning
needs, post-acute placement, and payer authorization requirements.
